title: The Case for Automated Hyperspecialization: Evidence from SAT
abstract: arXiv:2609.14836v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The software status quo is to use one system to process many different kinds of inputs. In contrast, we propose hyperspecialization: creating new software that is optimized for a single class of inputs. Hyperspecializing manually is anywhere from expensive to impossible. We conjecture that coding agents make automated hyperspecialization cheap, effective, and safe for problems with measurable performance and checkable output. This paper explores one such problem, SAT solving, by synthesizing hundreds of workload-specific SAT solvers at an average cost of \$37 each. Our specialists outperform their competition-winning, general-purpose cousins by 5$\times$ on average, and by over $10\times$ on a quarter of benchmark families. A general-purpose solver constructed from over a hundred of our prototype hyperspecialists won the SAT track at the 2026 SAT Competition.

translated_title: 自动化超专业化的论证：来自SAT求解的证据
translated_abstract: 软件行业的现状是使用一个系统来处理多种不同类型的输入。与之相反，我们提出了“超专业化”的概念：创建针对单一类别输入进行优化的新软件。手动进行超专业化的成本从高昂到几乎不可能。我们推测，对于性能可测量且输出可验证的问题，编程智能体能够使自动化超专业化变得廉价、有效且安全。本文探讨了其中一个问题——SAT求解，以每个平均37美元的成本合成了数百个针对特定工作负载的SAT求解器。我们的专业化求解器平均比赢得竞赛的通用求解器快5倍，在四分之一的基准测试族上快超过10倍。由我们一百多个原型超专业化求解器构建的通用求解器赢得了2026年SAT竞赛的SAT赛道冠军。
tldr: 本文提出“超专业化”理念，利用编程智能体以平均每个37美元的成本自动合成数百个针对特定工作负载的SAT求解器，其性能平均比竞赛级通用求解器快5倍，由此构建的求解器更赢得了2026年SAT竞赛冠军。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "automated hyperspecialization," using coding agents to synthesize hundreds of workload-specific SAT solvers at ~$37 each, achieving 5× average speedups over competition-winning general-purpose solvers, with a solver built from these specialists winning the 2026 SAT Competition.
